# Consensus-Illusion Detection: Sovereign Swarm Protocol Spec

## 0. Problem reduction

Naive majority voting treats `count(same answer) ≥ k` as consensus. A correlated hallucination defeats this: N agents emit byte-identical garbage because of (a) echo/copy, (b) shared seeds, (c) shared defective corpus/teacher, (d) shared prompt defect. The invariant we enforce:

> **Accept "consensus" only if ≥ k agents provably arrived at the identical answer through causally isolated, nonce-diverged, evidence-verifiable derivations, and the agreement probability under the measured coincidence budget of those agent lineages is below ε.**

Everything below makes each clause a byte-checkable predicate.

---

## 1. Exact state machine

**Round states:** `OPEN → FROZEN → REVEALED → AUDITED → SETTLED`
**Per-agent slots:** `INVITED → COMMITTED → REVEALED → AUDIT_PASS | AUDIT_FAIL`

| Transition | Guard | Action (bytes written) |
|---|---|---|
| OPEN→FROZEN | `now_seq ≥ freeze_seq` **or** all N commits received | Append `LedgerRow(kind=frozen)` |
| FROZEN→REVEALED | coordinator relays all buffered Reveals in commit-seq order | Relay rows in ledger |
| REVEALED→AUDITED | run verifier `V(transcript)` | Append `Verdict` |
| AUDITED→SETTLED | verdict signature verified | Round file closed |

**Storage:** append-only file `rounds/<rid_hex>.log`. Record framing: `[len:uint32][record_bytes]…`. Records are the messages below plus ledger rows. Settlement = presence of a validly-signed Verdict as final record. **No wall-clock timestamps anywhere** — total order is coordinator-assigned `seq:uint64` on receipt. This is what makes byte-identity achievable across machines.

---

## 2. Data shapes (CBOR, RFC 8949 §4.2.1 core-deterministic)

Global rules: map keys in canonical order, no indefinite lengths, **floats forbidden**, strings NFC, Ed25519 sigs over `dcbor(msg_minus_sig)`.

```text
rid      = bstr(16)          # 128-bit round id
aid      = bstr(8)           # agent id
nonce n  = bstr(16)          # per-agent, per-round, agent-generated

Seal = { t:"seal", rid, qhash:bstr(32), freeze_seq:uint64,
         kmin:uint, smin:uint, kindep:uint,
         tauq:uint16,          # τ×2^16, default 32768 (τ=0.5)
         epsnum:uint32,        # ε = epsnum/2^32, default 4096 (ε=2⁻²⁰)
         canon_id:text,        # "txt-v1"|"bin-v1"|"num-v1"
         toolset_id:text, calib_ver:text,
         lineages:[{aid, fp:bstr(32), dsroot:bstr(32)}],
         seq }

Commit = { t:"commit", rid, aid, c:bstr(32), seq, sig }   # c = SHA-256(dcbor({n,ans,trace}))

Step   = { i:uint, op:text, arg:bstr, oh:bstr(32),
           em:bool,           # true iff σ_i influenced oh
           ph:bstr(32) }      # ph_i = SHA-256(ph_{i-1} || dcbor(step minus ph)), ph₀ = rid||aid

Reveal = { t:"reveal", rid, aid, n, ans:bstr, trace:[Step], sig }

Verdict= { t:"verdict", rid, st:uint(0=REJECT,1=ACCEPT),
           acc:[aid], why:uint32, pv:uint128,
           logh:bstr(32), seq, sig }   # logh = SHA-256(concat all prior record bytes)

LedgerRow = { t:"ledger", seq, kind:"recv"|"relay"|"frozen",
              dst:aid|"*", src:aid|"coord", ref_seq }
```

**Determinism hooks baked into the shapes:**
- Tool execution seed: `σ(step) = SHA-256(n ∥ rid ∥ step.i)`. Injected by executor, never inside `arg`. Replay recomputes it from revealed `n`.
- `canon("txt-v1")`: NFC → strip `[ \t\n\v\f\r]` at ends → collapse internal runs to `0x20` → Unicode-15.1 casefold → UTF-8.
- **Agreement := `canon(ans_i) == canon(ans_j)` as raw bytes.** Nothing fuzzy survives.
- `p_agree(ℓ_a,ℓ_b)` stored as `uint32` numerator over 2³², pinned by `calib_ver` in the Seal.

---

## 3. Verifier `V: transcript → Verdict` (pure function, fixed order)

Checks C0–C7 in order; first failure sets `why`; group evaluation order: `(size desc, canon-bytes asc)`.

```
C0 SIG:      every record's Ed25519 sig valid; logh matches replay.
C1 BIND:     ∀ Reveal r: ∃ Commit with c == SHA-256(dcbor({r.n,r.ans,r.trace})) ∧ same aid.
             Duplicate aid in commits ⇒ why=4.
C2 CAUSALITY:∀ committed i: relay_seq(any Reveal → i) > commit_seq(i),
             ∧ relay_seq(Seal → i) < commit_seq(i).  Else why=3.   (read from LedgerRows)
C3 GROUPING: partition Revealed agents by canon(ans). Candidate groups |S| ≥ kmin, else why=5.
C4 PAIR AUDIT, ∀ i<j ∈ S:                                   else why=6
   P1 n_i ≠ n_j            (collision ⇒ drop higher aid, recount)
   P2 dcbor(trace_i) ≠ dcbor(trace_j)
   P3 G = {g : step g has em=true in both}; G ≠ ∅ ∧ ∃ g∈G: oh_i(g) ≠ oh_j(g)
      ∧ match_fraction((i,op,arg,oh) tuples) ≤ 0.9        (template-echo guard)
   P4 REPLAY: ∀ steps: SHA-256(tool(op,arg,σ)) == oh ∧ ph-chain recomputes. Fail ⇒ why=7, drop agent.
C5 LINEAGES: |distinct fp in S| ≥ smin                       else why=8
C6 SPUR:     anchor i₀ = min aid in S;
             spur_num = Π_{j∈S∖{i₀}} p_agree_num(ℓ_{i₀},ℓ_j)   (u128, early-abort)
             accept iff spur_num ≤ epsnum × 2^{32(|S|-2)}      else why=9, pv=spur_num
C7 COLLAPSE: EH_i = {oh : op=="cite"}; edges weighted ⌊Jaccard(EH_i,EH_j)·2¹⁶⌋;
             union-find over edges ≥ tauq (processed w desc, then aid-pair asc);
             component count ≥ kindep                          else why=10
ACCEPT: st=1, acc=S in aid order; else st=0 with first-failing why.
```

`why` codes: 0 ok, 1 sig, 2 unbound, 3 causality, 4 dup, 5 no-majority, 6 pair-copy/correlated-path, 7 replay-fail, 8 lineage-spread, 9 spur-budget, 10 evidence-collapse.

**Why each channel dies:** echo ⇒ C2 (couldn't see peers pre-commit) or C1 (can't change answer post-commit). Shared seed ⇒ P1/P3 (distinct nonces force distinct σ, hence distinct oh at entropy-mixed steps). Shared defective corpus ⇒ C6/C7 (measured coincidence budget + evidence-set overlap collapses witnesses). Fabricated evidence ⇒ P4.

---

## 4. Acceptance tests (byte-identity proofs)

**T1 — Golden vectors.** 32 frozen transcripts (`golden/NNNN.log`) with frozen `sha256(vbytes)` expectations, covering every `why` code ≥2×. Assert equality. Run under Python and Rust reference impls; bytes must match cross-language.

**T2 — Differential property test.**
```python
@given(seed=st.integers(0, 1000))
def test_byte_identity(seed):
    T  = gen_round(seed, corruptors=[copy_echo, shared_seed, late_commit,
                                     forged_oh, unicode_ligature, evidence_overlap])
    v1 = ref_verify(copy.deepcopy(T)); v2 = iut_verify(copy.deepcopy(T))
    assert sha256(dcbor(v1)) == sha256(dcbor(v2)) == GOLDEN_IF_SEED_IN_FIXTURE
```

**T3 — Near-miss negatives (proves the byte-identity check bites).** Mutate the winning answer by one canonicalization-visible byte — `ﬁ`→`fi`, trailing `U+00A0`, `0x0A`↔`0x20` run — assert verdict flips to exactly `why=5`.

**T4 — Order-independence.** Permute arrival order of Reveals (coordinator reassigns identical seqs per ledger replay) → identical `vbytes`.

**T5 — Separation operating characteristic.**
- Poisoned-swarm simulation: 7 agents, shared defective retrieval index, all agree on wrong A. Naive majority accepts; this pipeline must emit `why=9` or `why=10` on ≥99% of 1000 trials (using `p_agree` from the adversarial probe suite).
- Control swarm: independent errors → accept on ≥99%.

**T6 — Re-audit closure.** Independent auditor recomputes `logh` and reruns `V` → byte-identical Verdict.

**Calibration feed for C6:** probe suite of trap queries per known shared-failure mode (memorized-wrong facts, retrieval traps, tokenizer traps); `p_agree(a,b) = ceil_to_2⁻³²(wrong-coincidence rate)`; recalibrated on every checkpoint change; version pinned in Seal.

---

## 5. Honest boundary (one paragraph, no hedging needed elsewhere)

Byte-identity of the **decision** is a hard property: pure function, integer-only math (fixed-point 2³² rationals, early-abort products), no clocks or floats, canonical encodings, fixed iteration orders — verified by T1/T2/T4. Separation **strength** is conditional: a novel shared defect absent from the probe suite degrades gracefully to residual risk bounded by ε *given probe coverage*, and the round record embeds the exact quantities (`p_agree` version, spur product, collapse components)
reasoning:
The user wants a concrete, exact solution to the "consensus-illusion detection" problem: distinguishing true agreement from N correlated hallucinations in a swarm/flock consensus setting. They want:

1. The exact state change / data shape
2. An acceptance test that proves byte-identity
3. Concrete, exact, grounded — no fluff

This is a hard distributed-systems + ML problem. Let me think about what "consensus illusion" means: N agents all produce the same answer, but they're correlated — e.g., same training data, same prompt leakage, shared cache, one agent's output copied to others, or a common upstream failure mode. Naive majority voting counts N identical wrong answers as consensus. True consensus should mean independent derivation reaching the same result.

Key insight: You cannot prove independence post-hoc without provenance. The fix is to make independence a first-class, verifiable property of the message itself: each vote must carry (a) an independent randomness nonce that shaped its computation path, (b) a commitment chain proving it didn't read other agents' outputs before committing, and (c) enough evidence (intermediate artifacts) that a verifier can check the answer was derived, not echoed.

Let me design this concretely.

## Core mechanism

**Problem statement**: Swarm of N agents answers query Q. We must accept "consensus" only if at least k agents independently derived the same answer A, where "independently" means: no causal path existed by which agent i's answer could have been influenced by agent j's answer or by any shared correlated source beyond the declared task inputs.

**Correlated hallucination channels**:
1. **Copy/echo**: agent j saw agent i's output.
2. **Shared seed**: identical RNG seeds → identical sampling paths → identical errors.
3. **Common teacher**: all agents distilled from the same model / same retrieval corpus with same defect.
4. **Prompt coupling**: same system prompt bug steers all to same wrong answer.

Detection strategy per channel:
1. Commit-reveal ordering + causal isolation proof (each agent commits hash of (Q, personal_nonce) BEFORE seeing any peer traffic; reveal after).
2. Per-agent unique entropy: verifier injects distinct nonce n_i; agent must incorporate n_i into computation such that intermediate states differ. Identical intermediates across two agents with different nonces ⇒ copy or degenerate path.
3. Heterogeneity requirement: agents must be drawn from disjoint lineage classes (different checkpoints/fine-tunes), declared and attested. Correlation budget: pairwise answer-agreement probability under independence must be estimated from a calibration set.
4. Evidence-carrying votes: each vote carries intermediate artifacts (e.g., for arithmetic/reasoning: the trace; for retrieval: retrieved doc hashes; for classification: logit vectors). Verifier re-derives.

But we need something *exact and testable*, byte-identity provable. So define the state machine and data shape precisely.

### State change

Define a `ConsensusRound` object with explicit states:

```
IDLE → SEALED → DERIVE → COLLECT → AUDIT → ACCEPTED | REJECTED
```

State transitions with exact preconditions:

- IDLE→SEALED: coordinator publishes Q plus round_id, deadline T_commit, and per-agent nonce commitments? No — better: coordinator generates nonce n_i = H(round_id || agent_id || master_salt), gives n_i privately to agent i, and publishes H(n_i). Actually simpler: each agent generates own nonce, publishes commitment c_i = H(n_i || agent_pubkey) before receiving any peer data. Coordinator enforces: agent's DERIVE phase network access restricted to input channel only (attestation: signed receipt from network guard that no inter-agent packets were delivered to agent i between commit time and reveal time).

Hmm, but "no hedging" — pick one concrete design. Let me go with:

**Phase 0 — SEAL**: Coordinator broadcasts `Seal{round_id, Q_hash, T_reveal, k, N, lineage_manifest}`. Lineage manifest maps agent_id → {model_fingerprint, checkpoint_hash, fine-tune_dataset_merkle_root, sampler_seed_policy}. Constraint: at most m agents per lineage class where m ≤ ceil(N / L_classes)... keep simple: pairwise lineage distance ≥ d_min enforced.

**Phase 1 — COMMIT**: Agent i computes locally: picks random nonce n_i (128-bit), produces sealed envelope `E_i = Sig_i(H(Commit{n_i} || H(Q)))`... Actually the agent commits to its answer AND its nonce before seeing peers: `C_i = H(n_i ‖ A_i ‖ trace_i)` published at t < T_reveal. This prevents adaptive copying (you can't copy what you can't see, and you can't change your answer after seeing others because your commitment binds you).

**Phase 2 — REVEAL**: After T_reveal, all committed hashes are fixed. Agents publish `(n_i, A_i, trace_i, sig)`. Anyone verifies H(n_i‖A_i‖trace_i) == C_i.

**Phase 3 — INDEPENDENCE AUDIT** (the core novelty): For every pair (i,j) whose plaintext answers agree byte-wise, run the correlation battery:
  - **B1 Nonce-divergence**: trace_i ≠ trace_j as canonical bytes (their computation paths must differ since n_i ≠ n_j and both are required to mix n into the trace via a defined mixing step). If traces are byte-identical despite n_i ≠ n_j ⇒ REJECT with code COPY_OR_SEED_COLLISION (probability of true collision 2^-128 negligible; still treat as reject unless n_i == n_j which is impossible since n_i generated independently... well could collide; handle: if n_i == n_j then require re-run of those agents with fresh nonces — deterministic rule).
  - **B2 Path-distance**: define canonical trace as ordered list of typed steps. Compute structural edit distance D(i,j); require D ≥ D_min (calibrated threshold) OR at least one differing intermediate value at a step where divergence is expected under independence. Hmm, "expected divergence" needs grounding: under independence with distinct nonces, any step whose value depends on n must differ w.p. ≈ 1 − 2^-b where b is bits of n mixed into that step's value. So B2: find steps tagged `entropy-dependent`; require ≥ 1 such step differs between i and j. If all entropy-dependent steps match despite different nonces ⇒ either echo of a cached template or the nonce wasn't actually mixed ⇒ fail audit.
  - **B3 Evidence re-derivation**: verifier deterministically re-executes the trace skeleton: takes Q, n_i, and the declared tool-call sequence from trace_i, re-runs tools (retrieval etc.) and checks claimed outputs' hashes appear. This catches fabrication and catches shared-cache hallucination only partially — actually for hallucination-correlation: if two agents cite the same nonexistent source, B3 fails for both individually. But correlated-but-individually-valid errors pass B3. That's why we also have:
  - **B4 Calibration prior**: From a held-out calibration suite C of queries with known ground truth and known per-lineage error modes, estimate pairwise coincidence rate p_coinc(lineage_a, lineage_b) = P(A_a == A_b | both wrong, independent runs). Acceptance requires observed agreement count k to exceed the null hypothesis bound: P(X ≥ k) under X ~ Binomial(pairs, p_max_pair) ≤ ε. Concretely: compute p̂ from calibration, require k ≥ quantile_{1−ε}(Binomial(C(N,2)? no...

Hmm, careful: the right statistic isn't over pairs. Let me restate: Under the null "agents are correlated through some hidden shared cause," agreement among many agents is likely. Under independence, given per-agent correctness p_c and per-lineage error profiles, the probability of ≥k agreeing on a WRONG answer is bounded. Since ground truth is unknown at runtime, use: agreement on answer A is trustworthy iff P(≥k agents converge to A | the specific failure hypotheses) small. Practical exact rule: require (a) k ≥ k_min, (b) the k agreeing agents span ≥ s distinct lineage classes, (c) pairwise B1/B2 audits pass for ALL agreeing pairs, (d) each of the k passes B3, and (e) the agreement margin exceeds calibrated coincidence: k ≥ max(k_min, ceil(log(ε)/log(p̄_agree)) ) where p̄_agree is the max pairwise same-answer probability across the deployed lineages measured on adversarial calibration probes (queries engineered so that the known shared-defect produces a specific wrong answer). That last bit is nice: adversarial probe suite measures "how often do lineages a,b coincidentally land on the same wrong token" — gives numeric p_agree(a,b) ∈ [0,1]; acceptance threshold computed from these numbers exactly.

Also add **B5 anti-echo timing/order proof**: coordinator's transport guarantees no agent receives any peer packet until it has published its commitment; enforce via capability-token network policy + signed delivery logs. Byte-level: the delivery log is part of the round record; auditor replays it.

### Data shapes

Need exact schemas. Use CBOR (deterministic encoding, RFC 8949 core deterministic) for byte-identity. Define:

```
RoundID      = bstr(16)   // 128-bit
AgentID      = bstr(8)
Nonce        = bstr(16)
Answer       = bstr       // canonicalized answer payload
Trace        = [Step]
Step         = {step_idx: uint, op: text, args: bstr, out_hash: bstr(32),
                ent_mix: bool /* whether nonce mixed */, prev_hash: bstr(32)}
Commitment   = bstr(32)   // SHA-256 over DeterministicCBOR({nonce, answer, trace})
```

Hash-chain inside trace: prev_hash links steps, out_hash binds tool outputs; final commit binds everything → tamper-evident, replayable.

Envelope messages:

```
Msg.COMMIT = {type:"commit", round, agent, c: bstr(32), ts, sig}
Msg.REVEAL = {type:"reveal", round, agent, nonce, answer, trace, sig}
Msg.VERDICT= {type:"verdict", round, status, accepted_set:[agent], audit_log_hash, sig}
```

Canonicalization: CBOR core deterministic; strings NFC-normalized; floats banned (use rational pairs or scaled ints) — important for byte-identity. Answer equivalence for "agreement": byte-identity after applying the declared `answer_canon` function (e.g., trim whitespace, lowercase for text tasks, or exact bytes for payloads). To avoid ambiguity: agreement ⇔ canon(A_i) == canon(A_j) byte-wise. And the acceptance test proves byte-identity of the whole verdict record across independent auditors.

### Acceptance test that proves byte-identity

Two levels:
1. **Byte-identity of the decision procedure**: Given the same round transcript T (ordered list of msgs), any two implementations of the verifier produce the identical VERDICT record, byte-for-byte. How to guarantee: verdict computation is a pure function V(T) specified as deterministic pseudocode with fixed iteration order (sort by (round, agent)), fixed hash alg (SHA-256), fixed CBOR deterministic encoding, fixed tie-breaks. Test: property-based test generating R random valid transcripts; run reference implementation and implementation-under-test; assert sha256(cbor(verdict_ref)) == sha256(cbor(verdict_impl)) for all R. Also golden vectors: fixed transcripts with recorded verdict bytes.

2. **Byte-identity of accepted answers**: consensus claim "these agents agree" is proven by showing canon(A_i) bytes identical across the accepted set — trivially checked by equality, but the test must demonstrate the checker rejects near-misses (unicode confusables, trailing whitespace, float repr differences) — negative tests included.

Also the statistical acceptance test: given calibration matrix P (pairwise coincidence probabilities) and observed pattern, compute the exact binomial/Poisson-binomial tail; verdict includes the computed p-value as a fixed-point number so byte-identity extends to the numeric decision. To keep byte-exactness, specify p-value computation in integer arithmetic (Poisson-binomial via DP with rational arithmetic, rounded to fixed-point 10^-12, ties broken toward REJECT).

Let me now write the actual pseudocode for the verifier V(T):

```python
def verify(T):
    seal = T.seal
    commits = [m for m in T.msgs if m.type=="commit"] sorted by (ts, agent)
    reveals = ...
    # 1. binding check
    for r in reveals:
        c = sha256(dcbor({r.nonce, r.answer, r.trace}))
        assert exists commit with commit.c == c and commit.agent == r.agent
    # 2. causality check: every commit.ts < min(reveal broadcast ts) ... 
    #    more precisely: commit of agent i must be logged as received by coordinator
    #    before any reveal from agent j≠i was available on agent i's ingress (delivery log)
    # 3. group by canon(answer); candidate groups G with |G| >= k_min
    # 4. for each pair in G: 
    #     B1: ni != nj and trace_i != trace_j (byte compare of dcbor(trace))
    #         if ni == nj -> mark pair for forced re-run; if re-run not possible => reject group
    #     B2: exists step s in trace_i tagged ent_mix=true with matching step in j
    #         (same step_idx & op) and out_hash(s,i) != out_hash(s,j)
    #     B3: replay: for each step: tool_replay(op,args) hash == out_hash
    #         (tools must be deterministic given (args, nonce-mixed seed))
    #     B4: lineage check: |distinct lineages in G| >= s_min;
    #         poisson_binomial_tail(P_matrix, |G|, pattern) <= eps_fixed
    # 5. verdict: ACCEPT(group with lexicographically smallest canon bytes among passing groups)
    #    tie impossible because groups partition by canon bytes; if multiple groups pass,
    #    choose largest size, then smallest canon bytes (deterministic).
```

Edge rules to make it fully deterministic: duplicate commits from same agent → reject agent; commit after T_reveal → reject agent; missing reveal by T_final → drop agent (not reject whole round unless remaining < k_min).

Now the acceptance test proving byte-identity. Provide a concrete pytest-style harness:

```python
def test_verdict_byte_identity():
    for seed in range(1000):
        T = gen_random_transcript(seed, corruptors=[copy_echo, shared_seed, unicode_confusable, late_reveal])
        v1 = ref_verify(deepcopy(T))
        v2 = impl_under_test(deepcopy(T))
        assert sha256(dcbor(v1)) == sha256(dcbor(v2))
        # and cross-language: golden file
```

Plus golden vectors: `golden/round_0001.bin` → `golden/round_0001.verdict.hex` asserted equal.

And a negative test proving the detector actually separates correlated hallucinations: construct synthetic swarm where all agents share a defective retrieval index; naive majority accepts; our pipeline must emit REJECT with code CORR_HALLUC when the shared defect is detectable... wait — can it? If all agents genuinely independently derive the same wrong answer from the same bad corpus, B1–B3 pass (traces differ, evidence validates against the same bad corpus). Detection there comes from B4: the calibration/adversarial-probe layer must know that lineage set {a,b,c} has elevated mutual coincidence p_agree above threshold, forcing larger k or rejection. So honesty: the mechanism converts "unknown correlation" into "measured correlation budget." If a novel shared defect appears that wasn't probed, it's caught only probabilistically — mitigate with rotating adversarial probes and requiring lineage diversity. I should state that plainly: byte-identity is guaranteed for the decision procedure; separation guarantee is statistical with explicitly bounded false-accept probability ε given the calibration assumption, and the round record embeds the exact p-value so downstream consumers can apply their own bar.

Actually, one more strong idea to catch shared-corpus hallucinations at runtime: require each agent to include in its trace the content-addressed hashes of external evidence used (retrieval chunk hashes). Then the verifier checks: if the k agreeing agents' evidence-hash sets intersect heavily (e.g., > τ fraction shared), the agreement is downgraded to "single-source corroboration," counted as effective independence weight w = 1/(effective sources), not N. Exact rule: effective_k = Σ over agents 1/|overlap-weight|... make it crisp: build graph G on accepted candidates, edge (i,j) weighted by Jaccard(evidence_hashes_i, evidence_hashes_j); connected components with edge weight > τ collapse to one independent witness; require collapsed witness count ≥ k_indep. That's exact, computable, deterministic (with fixed ordering for union-find ties). 

So the final acceptance predicate:

ACCEPT iff all of:
1. Commitment integrity: ∀ revealed i: ∃ commit binding, sig valid.
2. Causal isolation: ∀ i: ingress log shows zero peer reveals before i's commit timestamp; seal received before commit.
3. Agreement: |{i : canon(A_i)=A*}| ≥ k_min for some A*.
4. Pairwise audit for all agreeing pairs: nonce-distinct, trace-distinct, ≥1 ent-mix step diverges, B3 replay clean.
5. Lineage spread: ≥ s_min distinct lineage classes among agreeing set; pairwise p_agree(a,b) product bound satisfied: Π p_agree over the set's lineage multiset ≤ ε (or equivalently collapsed-witness statistic).
6. Evidence de-duplication: collapsed independent witnesses ≥ k_indep with Jaccard threshold τ.
7. Determinism: verdict bytes = sha256 over canonical verdict CBOR, reproducible.

Numbers: pick defaults N≥7, k_min=4, s_min=3, τ=0.5, ε=2^-20, nonce=128-bit, D thresholds etc. Give exact sizes.

Byte layout specifics: CBOR deterministic profile: map keys sorted by encoded byte length then lexicographic? RFC 8949 deterministic: keys sorted by their encoded representation (length-first for the encoded key bytes... actually core deterministic sorting: shorter encoded key first, then bytewise). Just say "RFC 8949 Section 4.2.1 core deterministic encoding; map keys in canonical order; no indefinite lengths; floats forbidden."

Timestamps: use logical sequence numbers instead of wall clock to keep byte-identity across machines! Important: wall-clock in records breaks reproducibility. So the transcript uses coordinator-assigned monotonic seq_no per message, not timestamps. Delivery/causality uses seq numbers. Good detail — include it.

Signature: Ed25519 over dcbor(msg_without_sig). Agent pubkey pinned in lineage manifest.

Trace mixing spec: each step computes `step_seed = SHA-256(nonce || round_id || step_idx)`; tools receive step_seed as their RNG seed; ent_mix=true iff step_seed influences out_hash. Replay uses the same formula → deterministic. Two agents with different nonces will almost surely diverge at the first ent-mix step; identical out_hash across all ent-mix steps with different nonces ⇒ 2^-b per step evidence of copying; rule: any single ent-mix step collision is allowed only if step has b<32 bits influence... simpler exact rule: require ≥1 ent-mix step with ≥64 bits of nonce influence and differing out_hash; if none differs → pair flagged CORRELATED. Also cap: if MORE than 90% of steps byte-match, flag even if ent steps differ (template echo).

Hmm wait, there's subtlety: legitimate traces may legitimately be mostly identical (same tool sequence, similar outputs) — that's fine, that's convergence. The discriminator is the nonce-seeded divergence points. Good.

Poisson-binomial exact tail in integers: probabilities as rationals with denominator 2^32 (fixed point Q1.31?). Specify: all p_agree values quantized to multiples of 2^-32; DP over Bernoulli indicators computing distribution of W = number of "spurious agreements" ... honestly the cleaner formulation: For the agreeing set S of size m spanning lineages ℓ_1..ℓ_m, null hypothesis H_spur: all m agree by chance with pairwise coincidence probs. Model: probability that m independent draws all coincide = Π over structure... For simplicity and defensibility: use the maximum pairwise p within the set, p* = max_{i<j∈S} p_agree(ℓ_i,ℓ_j), and require m such that (p*)^{m−1} · C ≤ ε where C is a combinatorial factor for "some answer collides"... To stay exact and implementable: define spur_prob(S) = Π_{j=2..m} p_agree(ℓ_1, ℓ_j) (chain bound, union-bound style: probability that each subsequent agent lands on agent 1's answer). Require spur_prob(S) ≤ ε. All in uint64 fixed point: p stored as u32 numerator over 2^32; product in u128; compare to ε_num over 2^32·... fine — spell it as integer ops.
